en.title: Feminine Adjectives and Stress Shift
en.summary: Learn how Romanian feminine adjectives add a syllable and move the stress to a new sound.

sections.title: The sound
paragraphs: Look at the masculine word (frumos) /fruˈmos/. It has two beats. The stress is at the end. Now listen to the feminine word (frumoasă) /fru.moˈa.sə/. The word grows longer. It gains an extra beat. The main stress shifts forward onto the new sound.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Start with the male form (frumos) /fruˈmos/. Your voice punches the last part: -mos. To say (frumoasă) /fru.moˈa.sə/, open your mouth wider in the middle. Slide from 'o' to 'a'. Put your loudest voice right on that vowel pair. End softly on the final sound.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: The letters o-a often make a sliding vowel sound. When you see the feminine ending, the beat changes. The letter ă sits at the end. It sounds like the first vowel in 'about'. Keep that last sound short and weak. Push the loudness onto the sliding vowels before it.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not keep the stress on the old masculine beat. If you say (frumoasă) /fru.moˈa.sə/ with old stress, people might not understand. Do not drop the final weak vowel. Give each beat its own time. Move your voice to the middle vowels and finish gently.
